body:
<!-- plain-summary -->
Wyrd proves its correctness partly inside a deterministic simulator that replays every timing accident on demand. The current backends (redb, and TiKV via the M4 branch work) participate in that story; FoundationDB's driver cannot run inside the simulator directly, because it is a C library with its own network thread. This issue decides and implements how the FDB backend joins the simulation/trait-pinning story so it is held to the same standard as the backends it replaces.

## What

Give `metadata-fdb` a DST story with the same strength as the TiKV backend's, mirroring **M4.7 (#258)** and the answered fidelity question (#264):

1. **The constraint.** The `foundationdb` crate binds `libfdb_c`, which spawns its own network thread and does non-deterministic real I/O — it can never run under Wyrd's deterministic simulator without violating the seed-determinism discipline (ADR-0035). The same class of problem was faced for TiKV (an await-inside-commit backend) and answered with the simulated-backend / contract-harness split (#264, #447: the simulator drives the trait against a DST-resident implementation; the real driver is held to the *same executable contract* out-of-sim).
2. **Contract-harness leg (required).** The shared `metadata-conformance` suite (`run_all`, all 7 contracts — the shared executable contract, evolving implementation-first during the port and consolidated in #437 afterwards) is the equivalence anchor: the DST-resident store and the real `metadata-fdb` driver pass the identical suite, so what DST proves about the trait transfers to the FDB concrete to the extent the contract pins it.
3. **Simulated-FDB leg (decide).** Decide whether the DST-resident model needs FDB-*shaped* failure semantics beyond the generic store: optimistic conflict at commit time (the 1020 `not_committed` class surfacing as `Conflict` on conditional batches), and the 1021 `commit_unknown_result` ambiguity (commit landed or not, observer must not assume either). The 1021 mode is the one genuinely new failure shape FDB introduces — a DST nemesis that returns "unknown" on commit and later reveals either outcome would let the simulator search the ambiguity space the real fault battery (#442) can only sample.
4. **Fix-forward with #258.** If #258 lands a simulated-TiKV / contract-harness structure on the M4 branch, reuse its skeleton — the FDB model should be a second parametrization, not a second framework.

## Acceptance criteria

- A recorded decision (in the issue or a short doc note) on simulated-FDB vs contract-harness-only, with the 1021-ambiguity question answered explicitly.
- The DST suite runs green with the chosen structure; `metadata-fdb` passes the identical `metadata-conformance` suite the DST-resident store passes.
- If the simulated-FDB leg is built: a DST scenario that exercises commit-ambiguity (1021-shaped) and shows no invariant violation across seed sweeps.
- No `libfdb_c` symbol is reachable from any DST build target (the sim graph stays pure and deterministic).

## Sequencing

Depends on #438 (the driver); #437 consolidates the contract docs afterwards. Coordinates with #258 (M4.7) on the shared structure. Feeds #442 — the battery samples what the simulator searches. Targets `main` after `feat/m4-production-metadata-backend` merges.

milestone.title: Metadata Store FoundationDB
milestone.description: Production distributed MetadataStore backend on FoundationDB — the chosen production backend per ADR-0042. metadata-fdb behind the fdb feature (implementation-first per ADR-0002; contract docs consolidated afterwards in #437), libfdb_c packaging + wyrd:fdb image, dev/CI harness, deploy profiles, go/no-go fault+contention battery, and the TiKV development stand-down once FDB is the default. (Renamed from metadata-client.)

title: metadata-fdb DST story: pin the MetadataStore trait for an FFI backend (contract harness + simulated-FDB / 1021-ambiguity question; mirrors M4.7)
